newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says Japan unfairly blocking fruit imports.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says Japan unfairly blocking fruit imports.

text.p: The United States said Japan is unreasonably blocking imports of a variety of U.S. apples and other fruit and asked for justification of the action.

In a letter released late Saturday to Japanese Trade Minister Shunpei Tsukahara, Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky, who was in Seattle attending a trade ministers meeting, and U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said discussions on health standards for certain kinds of U.S. apples have been "frustrating and unsuccessful."

The letter said Japan was blocking imports of a number of U.S. apples on the basis of how they are treated for codling moth when they accept the same variety of apples from New Zealand, which uses the same method of treatment as U.S. producers.
"We have encountered the same difficulties in seeking access to the Japanese market for new varieties of US cherries and nectarines," the letter added.

The letter asked for Japanese justification for excluding the imports no later than October 7. In January 1995, Japan agreed to import red and golden delicious apples from the United States and U.S. producers are seeking to export more varieties of the fruit.
